rationale: Pearson connectivity varies strongly with scanner and protocol, and the score only compares subjects within a site. This version standardizes each connectivity feature within its site (per-site mean and std) before the classifier. That removes the between-site shifts, so the L2 logistic regression is pushed toward the autism-vs-control differences that hold within each site. The site statistics use pooled train and test features but no labels, so sites that appear only in the test fold are handled too. Site is used only to harmonize features, never as a predictor.

I'm replacing the Fisher-z Pearson features with a tangent-space embedding of Ledoit-Wolf shrunk correlation matrices. The reference point is the Riemannian mean, computed on the training fold only. This was the strongest classic ABIDE pipeline (Abraham 2017). It respects the SPD geometry of connectivity matrices, and it whitens each subject relative to the group mean, which tends to reduce site and subject-level distortions. I haven't run it yet, so there's no new dev score.

Scoring is done within each site, so these shifts are pure noise to the classifier, and they use up its limited capacity in this regime where features far outnumber subjects. I'm adding one change: per-site standardization (a simple ComBat-style location/scale step) of the Fisher-z connectivity features before the same L2 logistic regression. Each site's mean and SD come from that site's pooled train+test features, which uses no labels. A site with fewer than 3 subjects falls back to the global scaling.
